band_change_evidence_test.required: >=2 independent sources with >=1 at sourceTier >=4, excluding self-published corporate material
band_change_evidence_test.detail: Human Rights Watch (tier 3, 2026-09-01), NPR (tier 2, 2026-05-23) and MercoPress (tier 2, 2026-03-31) are three independent, dated, within-period sources. No tier-4-or-above source (UN body, treaty body, court, international organisation) was located for Chile's 2026 conduct. Material that initially appeared to be a 2026 UN Special Procedures communication was re-fetched and found to be dated 2023; it was excluded. The band-crossing evidence bar is therefore NOT met and the band change is filed as unproven.

scoring_convention: Absence of disclosure scores 2, never 1. A score of 1 requires positive documented evidence of a specific failure. Absence is not evidence of harm.

anti_false_positive_screening.baseline_provenance: Published 62.5 was last reviewed on 2026-05-03 (research/digests/2026-05-03.md, Chile 62.5 -> 65.0 proposed, +2.5, sub-threshold confirmation) on pension-reform gender-equity evidence from the previous administration. rotation-state records last_assessed 2026-05-03, last_change_proposal null. APPLIED_CHANGES.md contains no Chile score entry. The published vector is near-uniform (seven of eight dimensions at exactly 3.5).
anti_false_positive_screening.stale_baseline_note: This proposal does NOT rest on a stale-baseline argument. It rests on documented conduct by the current government within the period: the regularisation freeze (2026-03-31), the first deportation flight (2026-04-17), two bills sent to Congress (2026-05-23), and the eight-amendment constitutional package submitted to the Senate (2026-08-18).
anti_false_positive_screening.directionality: Entity surfaced on NEGATIVE within-window evidence and this proposal is a DOWNGRADE. Direction matches the evidence.
anti_false_positive_screening.calibration_note: Part of the movement replaces a near-uniform seed vector with an evidence-based one. This is disclosed rather than presented as pure conduct. If the founder judges the calibration component dominant, the correct remedy is a cohort review of never-individually-assessed Established-band countries carrying near-uniform 3.5 vectors, not an isolated 20-point move on Chile.
anti_false_positive_screening.measures_absence_note: This movement measures documented conduct, not absence of disclosure. Two subdimensions (B1 self-sustainability, I3 internal consistency) rest on evidence gaps and were scored 3 on general institutional functioning rather than scored down.

key_evidence: Chile suspended a decree that would have regularised roughly 182,000 people who had already voluntarily registered with immigration authorities (MercoPress, 2026-03-31).
Two bills before Congress would criminalise irregular entry and limit migrants' access to social security benefits (NPR, 2026-05-23).

Eight constitutional amendments submitted to the Senate on 2026-08-18 would allow a "public security" state of emergency of up to 240 days without congressional approval, suspending freedom of movement and assembly (Human Rights Watch, 2026-09-01).

Chile’s GES/AUGE explicit health guarantees and CASEN survey remain genuine institutional strengths; Action (3.4) and Awareness (3.2) are scored accordingly and are the reason this is not a Developing-band outcome.
A claimed 2026 UN finding against Chile was re-fetched and proved to be dated 2023. It was excluded and did not score.

notes: FLAG FOR REVIEW — NOT A CLEAN DOWNGRADE. Two procedural reasons, neither of which disputes the underlying facts. (1) The BAND-CROSSING EVIDENCE TEST FAILED: no tier-4-or-above within-period source was located, so the Established-to-Functional crossing is not proven to the benchmark's own standard. (2) The -20.0 magnitude MIXES CONDUCT WITH SEED REPLACEMENT: the published 62.5 rested on a near-uniform vector (seven of eight dimensions at exactly 3.5) that had never been individually evidenced. Reporting the whole -20.0 as new Chilean misconduct would be factually wrong. RECOMMENDED REMEDY: handle Chile inside a cohort review of never-individually-assessed Established-band countries with near-uniform 3.5 vectors, rather than as an isolated move. If applied anyway, the applied record MUST state both that part of the movement replaces a seed and that no tier-4 source supports the band change. SEPARATE FINDING RECORDED IN THE ASSESSMENT: a purported 2026 UN Special Procedures communication to Chile was re-fetched and found to be dated 24 May 2023, on Global Detention Project pages dated 2023-06-01 and 2023-12-12; associated detention-period and healthcare/school data-sharing claims were excluded and did not score.
